# Unicode simple case-fold data

Engacer OS M14.3 uses Unicode 17.0.0 simple case-fold C/S records as its selected invariant file/registry identity profile. This is data, not a third-party compatibility runtime. Full multi-character and locale-specific Turkic folds and Unicode normalization are excluded. It does not claim identical NLS tables across all Windows releases.

The official versioned source and its SHA-256 are pinned in provenance.json. The raw research copy stays outside OneDrive; compilation uses the committed generated table without network access. `python tools/build/unicode143.py --source PATH` regenerates it and `--check` compares both generated bytes and metadata. The generator compresses 1,512 mappings into 209 arithmetic ranges: 3,344 read-only component bytes, excluding code/alignment. This is not total OS RAM.

Simple folding makes one-code-point case pairs comparable without expanding names or conflating canonically different Unicode sequences. Locale-based host conversion would make identity depend on the build machine. Full-fold expansion would also change the selected file-name semantics. UTF-16/UTF-8 conversion remains strict and bounded; malformed or over-budget input must refuse rather than truncate.

The [Unicode-3.0 license](LICENSE.txt) applies to the derived data and must accompany distributions using it. [Upstream data](https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/CaseFolding.txt), [upstream license](https://www.unicode.org/license.txt). Host codec/table checks are supporting evidence; native Windows path/registry qualification is separate M14.3 work.
